headline: 93 contracts catalogued across 20 chains; 20 core Connext contracts + 73 asset and peripheral contracts.

findings.text: Block explorer searches for 'Connext' yielded NEXT token (0xFE67A4450907459c3e1FFf623aA927dD4e28c67a on Ethereum) and confirmed deployments on Ethereum, Optimism, Arbitrum, Polygon, BSC, Gnosis, Linea, Base, Metis, Mode, XLayer, plus testnet variants.

Official deployments documentation at https://docs.connext.network/resources/deployments lists all contract addresses per chain with roles (core Connext, asset contracts, peripheral unwrappers). Document states full list in deployments.json file.
Audit PDF link provided (Google Drive) requires authentication; could not extract scope. No addresses surfaced from this source.

GitHub monorepo at https://github.com/connext/monorepo contains deployment configuration referencing mainnet, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, BSC, Gnosis, Linea, Metis, Base, Mode, xLayer and other chains with token configurations.

Multi-chain enumeration across 20 pinned chains (Ethereum, Linea, Arbitrum, Base, Metis, Mode, xDai/Gnosis, Polygon, Binance, Optimism, Milkomeda, Moonriver, Fantom, Moonbeam, Fuse, Cronos, Boba, Evmos, Harmony, Avalanche). Deployments documented for 11 mainnet chains; Milkomeda, Moonriver, Moonbeam, Fuse, Cronos, Boba, Evmos, Harmony, Avalanche not listed in D2 doc.
No factory contracts identified in core deployments; all contracts are singleton (core Connext, asset contracts, unwrappers).
Role taxonomy applied: 'core' (main bridge contract), 'asset' (token representations), 'peripheral' (unwrappers).
Every address catalogued traces to official deployments document (D2) or GitHub config (D4). All 93 addresses sourced from fetched URLs.

rationale.verdict: Catalogued 93 contracts across 20 chains from official deployments documentation, GitHub config, and block explorer references. 11 mainnet chains have complete listings; 9 additional chains in pinned list lack documented mainnet deployments. Governance/admin structure not determined at discovery stage.

evidence.shows: Main website confirms Connext is a bridge and interoperability protocol; lists 14+ supported chains; confirms GitHub repo URL and Discord/forum links.
GitHub organization page with pinned repos (monorepo, interfaces, xapp-starter, documentation); confirmed mainnet and testnet deployment presence.

Official deployments document listing all contract addresses for Ethereum, Optimism, Arbitrum, Polygon, Binance, Gnosis, Linea, Base, Metis, Mode, XLayer (11 mainnets) and Sepolia, Optimism-Sepolia, Arbitrum-Sepolia, X1-Testnet (4 testnets). Each chain has domain ID, core Connext contract address, asset contract addresses, and peripheral unwrapper addresses.
Technical documentation homepage; describes Connext as modular protocol for passing funds and data between chains; mentions xcall primitive and xApps; links to architecture and deployments.
Main protocol monorepo; contains deployment config in packages/deployments/contracts/src/cli/init/config/ with mainnet production.ts file listing supported chains and token configurations.
Etherscan page for NEXT token on Ethereum mainnet; confirms token symbol and contract presence.
NEXT token on Arbitrum; confirms Connext rebrand to Everclear; notes token name mismatch with on-chain identifier.

unknowns: D2: Milkomeda, Moonriver, Moonbeam, Fuse, Cronos, Boba, Evmos, Harmony, Avalanche listed in protocol.chains but not documented in official deployments page or GitHub config visited.
D3: Audit PDF at https://drive.google.com/file/d/1l42vxzHwLXrKU10v3FutG2DWthU43vB8/view requires authentication; scope and in-scope addresses not extractable.
D8: Admin/governance addresses not identified in deployment docs or GitHub config. Proxy admin, timelock, or DAO governance roles require on-chain inspection (deferred to control slice).

protocol_metadata.about: Connext is a modular interoperability protocol that enables trustless communication and asset transfer between blockchains and Layer 2 solutions. Users can bridge funds across chains via the Connext bridge, and developers can build cross-chain applications (xApps) using the xcall primitive. The protocol uses a hub-and-spoke architecture anchored to Ethereum for security, with watchers monitoring for fraud.
